You are a developer-relations researcher at a company that turns SaaS apps into tools AI agents can call.
Research ONE app and fill a strict JSON schema. Use web search. Prefer the vendor's own developer docs,
API reference, pricing page, and app-review/partner pages over blogs or aggregators.

App: Intercom
Category: Support and Helpdesk
Hint (may be misleading, verify it): intercom.com

Rules
1. Every field is an object: {"value": ..., "confidence": "high|med|low", "source_url": "..."}.
2. source_url must be a page you actually saw in search results for THIS field. Never construct or guess a URL.
   If you did not find one, set value "unknown", confidence "low", source_url null.
3. "unknown" is a correct, rewarded answer. An invented answer is the worst possible answer.
4. access_path = the most restrictive step needed to use the API in production, not just to read docs.
   Self-serve OAuth client + mandatory app review for production scopes => "app_review_required".
   Free docs but the useful endpoints need a paid plan => "paid_plan_required".
5. If the thing is a command-line tool or library with no hosted API, use api_type "cli_only",
   auth_methods ["none"], access_path "not_applicable_local", toolkit_bucket "local_or_sandbox_toolkit".
6. If the hint names a different product than the app (e.g. a parent platform), research the app itself and say so in main_blocker.
7. "OAuth requested" or "coming soon" is NOT shipped. Only report auth that is documented as available.
8. official_mcp = "official" only if the vendor itself publishes or documents the MCP server.
9. confidence: high = stated explicitly on a vendor docs page; med = inferred from vendor pages; low = third-party or memory.

Allowed enums
auth_methods (array): oauth2, api_key, basic, bearer_token, jwt, hmac_signature, session_login, none, unknown
access_path: self_serve_free, self_serve_trial, paid_plan_required, app_review_required, partner_or_sales_gated, no_public_api, not_applicable_local, unknown

base_url_model: fixed, per_tenant_subdomain, self_hosted_or_customer_host, regional, not_applicable, unknown

docs_quality: full_public_reference, partial_or_thin, none_public, unknown
test_account: free_tier_or_sandbox, trial_only, none, unknown

Return ONLY this JSON, no prose, no markdown fences:
{
  "one_liner": {...},        // what it does, max 15 words
  "auth_methods": {...},
  "access_path": {...},
  "api_type": {...},
  "api_breadth": {...},

Based on the search results, here's what I found about the official Intercom MCP server:

## Official Status

The Intercom MCP server is Intercom's official implementation of the Model Context Protocol, the open standard that lets AI applications talk to external systems. Intercom maintains one official server, reachable at https://mcp.intercom.com/mcp, with 13 tools.

## Current Ownership

Intercom runs an official remote MCP server at mcp.intercom.com, now maintained by Fin after Intercom's 2026 rebrand.

## Capabilities

It exposes your Intercom workspace to an assistant as a set of typed tools, so the AI can find and read support data on your behalf. It works with Claude, ChatGPT (OpenAI), and any other assistant or LLM that supports the Model Context Protocol.

The server provides tools for:
- Search and fetch functionality for conversations, contacts, companies, and help center articles, with the ability to create or update articles

## Authentication & Regional Support

It supports OAuth 2.0 or Bearer-token authentication and is available for US and EU hosted workspaces, with AU not yet supported.

I found comprehensive information about Intercom's authentication methods. Here's what the search results reveal:

## Authentication Methods

OAuth is for building public apps that access other people's Intercom data, while Access Tokens can be used for private apps, running scripts, or programmatically automating actions in your own workspace.

## Finding Your Access Token

You can find your Access Token in the Configure > Authentication section in your app within the Developer Hub. Your Access Token can give access to your private Intercom data and should be treated like a password.

## OAuth Setup

If you are building a public integration that will have access to other peoples' Intercom data you are required to set up OAuth. You'll first need your client_id and client_secret, which can be found on the Basic Information page for your app in the Developer Hub.

To get the Authorization Code, you need to redirect your user to: https://app.intercom.com/oauth?client_id=___&state=___

## Security Note

If an app provider asks you for your Access Token, please do not provide it. Instead, apps are required to use OAuth rather than asking users for Access Tokens.

These resources link to the official Intercom Developer Platform documentation for more detailed guidance on implementing either authentication method.

content.content:
# Intercom API Overview

**Base URL:** The production API server is located at `https://api.intercom.io`, with regional variants for Europe (`https://api.eu.intercom.io`) and Australia (`https://api.au.intercom.io`).

**API Type:** REST API. The documentation explicitly references "REST-api" endpoints and uses standard HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH).

**Breadth of Resources:** The Intercom API offers extensive coverage across multiple functional domains:

- **Messaging & Conversations:** Conversations, messages, replies, and conversation management
- **Contact Management:** Users, leads, contacts, companies, and segments
- **Knowledge Base:** Articles, internal articles, snippets, collections, and help centers
- **Support Operations:** Tickets, ticket types, teams, and macros
- **Customer Data:** Custom attributes, data attributes, data events, and audience management
- **Content & AI:** AI-powered content import sources, external pages, and Fin Agent capabilities
- **Administrative Functions:** Admin management, activity logs, away status, and office hours
- **Workflow & Automation:** Data connectors, workflows, and bulk actions
- **Analytics & Reporting:** Data export, event summaries, and reporting data export

The API encompasses approximately 40+ resource categories with hundreds of individual endpoints, making it a comprehensive platform for customer communication and engagement automation.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about Intercom developer hub app review submission and OAuth for production:

## App Review Submission Requirements

Public apps require setting up OAuth and submitting to the Intercom team for review. Both unlisted and listed apps must be submitted for review, which requires filling out the App Listing and App Partner Program pages in the Developer Hub and ensuring that all the requirements for each are met.

## OAuth Configuration for Production

Once development is done and OAuth is configured, in the Developer Hub of your Production app you can choose the listing type, provide installation URLs, and follow the steps outlined to submit it for review. Developers set up OAuth through the Developer Hub and must complete a review process before listing.

## Review Timeline and Scope Considerations

Every public app will need to be reviewed by the Intercom team, and these reviews typically take 7-14 days, but if your app is initially rejected you will need to make updates based on the feedback provided.

An important consideration: Over-privileged scopes are the most common reason that apps are initially rejected in the approval process, so you should only specify the scopes you definitely need for your use case, as these will go up for review when you submit your app for review.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about MCP on the Intercom Developer Platform:

## What is Model Context Protocol (MCP)?

MCP is a protocol that enables AI tools and applications to connect with Intercom's data and services in a secure, standardized way. It provides a structured method for AI models to find and retrieve Intercom data (conversations, contacts, etc.), access specific tools and functionality provided by Intercom, and maintain context about your Intercom workspace when working with AI assistants.

## Region Availability

The Intercom MCP server is available for US and EU hosted workspaces, while AU hosted workspaces are not yet supported.

## Available Tools

The Intercom MCP Server provides 14 tools for interacting with the Intercom API. These include tools for:
- Searching conversations with advanced filtering options
- Retrieving single conversations by ID with complete details
- Searching contacts by various attributes and getting complete contact information including custom attributes and location data

The search results indicate that Intercom has comprehensive documentation for MCP setup and implementation on their developer platform.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about Intercom pricing and API access:

## API Access Included in Plans

API access is included on all paid Intercom plans starting at $29/seat/month (Essential, billed annually). There are no per-call charges or API-specific credit costs on top of the plan subscription.

## Pricing Structure

The Essential plan starts at $29/seat/month on annual billing and includes Fin AI Agent and the full helpdesk. The seat tiers — Essential ($29), Advanced ($85), Expert ($132) per seat/month annually — are straightforward, but they're only the floor.

## Free Trial

A 14-day cardless free trial gives access to the full API during the trial, but there is no permanent free tier.

## Important Note on Add-ons

While API access is included, the real cost for a developer building on this API is not the API itself but the platform features the API operates within: Fin AI Agent charges ($0.99 per resolved outcome) and usage-based channel fees (email, SMS, WhatsApp).
